preamble: Denasalization of the glottalized alveolar nasal [nˀ] (Americanist n̓) to plain [d]. In Makah the Proto-Southern-Wakashan (PSW) nasals became voiced stops and the glottalized sonorants merged with the plain ones, lengthening the preceding vowel (Davidson 2002: 76, citing Jacobsen 1968). PSW *n̓ therefore appears as Makah d, while Nuu-chah-nulth keeps n̓: Nuu-chah-nulth čun̓a, Makah ču·da 'vulva'. The same correspondence recurs in suffixes listed by Davidson. For Quileute, Wikipedia's summary of Powell (1974) gives Proto-Chimakuan *n̓ > Quileute d or ʔd (Chemakum n or ʔn), without a word example. Ditidaht has the same plain d word-initially, where its glottalized d̓ cannot occur: Proto-Wakashan *n̓ak- 'look' gives Nuu-chah-nulth n̓ač- but Ditidaht and Makah dač- (Howe & Pulleyblank 2001). After a vowel Ditidaht keeps the glottalization as d̓.

languageExamples.context: Davidson (2002: 76): the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain sonorants in Makah, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (citing Jacobsen 1968); Nuu-chah-nulth keeps them; the nasal also became a stop, as plain *n did

examples.note: Davidson (2002: 76), ex. (127). The long u· before d is the compensatory lengthening.

languageExamples.context: Word-initially, where Ditidaht d̓ cannot stand: Werle (2010: 5) says glottalized b̓ d̓ must follow a vowel. Initial *n̓ gives plain d, merging with *n

examples.note: Howe & Pulleyblank (2001), ex. (30a), p. 22 of the accepted manuscript, citing Howe (1999). Makah also has dač-. Plain *naq- 'drink' gives Ditidaht and Makah daq-. Werle (2010: 9), ex. (23), has Ditidaht dačooʔł, Makah dačʔoł 'see'.
Werle (2010: 17), ex. (71), where the set illustrates vowel absence. Makah has duˑwiqs; its long uˑ reflects the lost glottalization of *w̓, not of *n̓.
